title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Collection; Comment Request
Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for Ciliate-Leaf Tickseed
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the ciliate-leaf tickseed (Coreopsis integrifolia), a plant species from Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the ciliate- leaf tickseed. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Plants and extend the Act's protections to the species.

title: Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Application for an Exemption From Liberty Bulk Transport, LLC, USDOT No. 3256390
summary: FMCSA announces its decision to grant an application from Liberty Bulk Transport, LLC, USDOT No. 3256390, (Liberty) for an exemption to allow it to operate commercial motor vehicles (CMVs) equipped with a module manufactured by Intellistop, Inc. (Intellistop). The Intellistop module is designed to pulse the required rear clearance, identification, and brake lamps from a lower-level lighting intensity to a higher-level lighting intensity 4 times in 2 seconds when the brakes are applied and then return the lights to a steady- burning state while the brakes remain engaged. The Agency has determined that granting the exemption to Liberty would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level of safety achieved by the regulation.

title: Technical Updates to the RCRA Hazardous Waste Permitting Regulations-Permitting Technical Updates Rule
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing technical updates to the regulations implementing the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) governing hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facilities (TSDFs), as well as associated permitting requirements. The proposal also includes a few conforming technical updates to the generator and transporter regulations. The RCRA hazardous waste TSDF permitting regulations have remained largely unchanged for over three decades, despite evolving standards and practices. Collectively, these revisions are intended to address inadvertent errors, remove obsolete references, reflect current information and standards, and implement targeted updates to the RCRA permitting regulations to improve clarity, consistency, and efficiency in the hazardous waste TSDF permitting program. Through a separate Federal Register document, EPA will be seeking input on areas in the RCRA permitting program and permitting regulations to consider for permitting policy or regulatory reform. This proposed rule helps clear the way for potential future regulatory actions that could improve implementation of the RCRA hazardous waste permitting program. It serves as a maintenance action and does not preclude the possibility of future permitting reform.

title: Significant New Use Rule on a Chemical Substance (P-24-195)
summary: EPA is proposing a significant new use rule (SNUR) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for a chemical substance that was the subject of a premanufacture notice (PMN) and is also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNUR requires persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of this chemical substance for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.
